artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(K_i)_{i \ge 1}$ be a sequence of compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$ such that $0 \in K_i$ for every $i$ and $\operatorname{diam}(K_i) \to 0$ as $i \to \infty$. Define the subsum set
$$S \;=\; \Big\{ \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} x_j \;:\; x_j \in K_j \text{ for each } j \ge 1 \Big\},$$
which converges since the diameters tend to $0$. For each $z \in S$, define the tail set
$$R_z \;=\; \Big\{ \sum_{j=n+1}^{\infty} x_j \;:\; n \ge 0,\; x_j \in K_j,\; z - \sum_{j=n+1}^{\infty} x_j \in S \Big\},$$
i.e.\ the collection of possible tail values arising in representations of $z$.

A representation of a complex number $z$ as an element of $S$ via a choice of $x_j \in K_j$ is called a \emph{radix-style representation} of $z$ (with digit sets $K_j$ and admissible tails in $R_z$).

Excluding the trivial case in which $S = \mathbb{C}$ holds vacuously, determine explicit and nontrivial conditions on the sequence of digit sets $(K_i)$ and on the associated tail sets $R_z$ which guarantee that every algebraic number $z \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ admits such a radix-style representation
$$z \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} x_j, \qquad x_j \in K_j.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly open question in a survey on subsums of null sequences (December 2020). No subsequent literature found that resolves it; the question of characterizing digit-set/tail conditions ensuring radix representability of all algebraic numbers in this setting appears to remain open.
